- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean or 0.5–1.0 price point.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.33) in recent days, model tends to overreact — adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of recent mean or 0.5–1.0 price point.
- After a sharp price spike (≥3% from prior 5-day high), model often overshoots — reduce forecast by 1–3% of spike magnitude or 0.5–1.5 price points.
- Model consistently underestimates downward moves in bearish sentiment cycles — add 0.5–1.0 price point buffer for 3–5 day bearish trends.
- Model overestimates upward moves in bullish sentiment cycles — subtract 0.5–1.0 price point buffer for 3–5 day bullish trends.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to lag by 1–2 days in reaction to sentiment shifts — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead by +0.5–1.0 price point if sentiment is trending.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >1.5σ above recent 18d mean, reduce by 0.5–1.0 price point; if <1.5σ below, increase by 0.5–1.0 price point.
- Sentiment volatility >0.33 in 3 consecutive days → reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% to avoid overfitting to noise.
